title: SiloFacet safeTransferFrom/safeBatchTransferFrom omit sibling's nonReentrant
description: Within SiloFacet the deposit-transfer group has asymmetric reentrancy guarding. `transferDeposit` (public, L140) and `transferDeposits` (external, L173) carry `fundsSafu noNetFlow noSupplyChange nonReentrant`. The ERC1155-standard siblings `safeTransferFrom` (L211) and `safeBatchTransferFrom` (L237) carry `fundsSafu noNetFlow noSupplyChange` but OMIT `nonReentrant`. They are in the same semantic group (move deposits/stalk between accounts).
impact: None exploitable. Both functions immediately route to `transferDeposit(...)`, which is itself `nonReentrant` and backed by the SHARED diamond reentrancy slot (s.sys.reentrantStatus). Any reentry attempt during the transfer is caught by the inner guard. The functions perform no external token transfer or callback of their own (deposits are internal accounting; no ERC1155 acceptance-hook callback to the recipient is invoked). The omission is a guard-consistency blemish, not a reachable reentrancy.

ite.intent: Apply the same nonReentrant guard to every external deposit-transfer entrypoint
ite.technique: safe* variants rely on the callee transferDeposit's guard rather than declaring their own; the asymmetry is cosmetic because the shared reentrant slot is set by the inner call
ite.evasion: No viable evasion: no external callback path exists in safe* before/after the guarded inner call

ice_chain.corrupted_state: none (reentry blocked by inner transferDeposit nonReentrant on the shared s.sys.reentrantStatus slot)
